answer: Delayed Cedar Handoff** Each new agent identity must complete a saffron-marked handoff: it receives a task, waits out a randomized delay drawn from a public distribution, then passes a verifiable result to an existing agent that signs the handoff. Identity activation requires a raven-stamped receipt from three independent handoffs across separate epochs. Duplicates must pay the full delay and compute cost per identity, so mass registration scales linearly in wall-clock time and worker attention rather than in cheap key generation.
